text:
Ingrid: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A on engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Posting the decisions and answers to the open questions.

Lee: Thanks! Can you confirm the release cadence again? There were mixed signals about speed vs safety.

Ingrid: Sure. We agreed on a predictable cadence:
- Major release train: every 2 weeks (Tue 09:00 PT deploy)
- Minor infra/ops patches: weekly (Thu)
- Hotfixes: ad-hoc using the emergency rollback playbook
Feature rollouts should use canary + staged percentages; non-runtime UX can be feature-flagged.

Matt: For the 2-week train, what is the freeze window for runtime/model-serving changes?

Ingrid: Freeze window is 48 hours before the deploy for anything touching runtime or model-serving infra. Branches touching non-critical UI can land and be gated by flags.

Sofia: On oncall rotations: 2-week rotations, primary + secondary. Escalation: primary -> secondary -> oncall manager (20m) -> SRE lead. Targets: acknowledge within 10 min, mitigation/rollback attempt within 30 min for regressions. If hosted customer SLA is impacted, notify CS within 1 hour.

Matt: Are these pager targets the same for Dedicated enterprise customers? Sales asks about response SLAs.

Sofia: Default internal pager SLO is 10 min. Enterprise/Dedicated customers can have contract-specific times in the SOW.

Emily: For model rollouts, what are the canary windows and auto-rollback thresholds? Missed that slide.

Priya: Canary policy we will start with:
- 5% for 1 hour, then 25% for 6 hours, then 100% if no issues.
- Monitor: model-quality evals, token-error rate, user error-rate, latency p95/p99.
- Auto-rollback triggers include:
  - quality regression > 5% on labeled evals
  - user error rate > 2x baseline
  - p99 latency increase > 40% or p95 spike > 200ms over baseline
Teams should treat these as defaults; ML will tune per-model.

Lee: Where are the canonical playbooks stored? Ops needs links.

devbot: Release playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/release-cadence
Canary policy: https://redwood.internal/platform/canary-policy
Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-response

Matt: Sales follow-up: how do SLA credits work for hosted API downtime? Is there a public doc we can point customers to?

Ingrid: Public-facing SLA summary exists for hosted customers (99.9% monthly uptime). Credits are pro-rata after incident classification and investigation. Detailed contract terms for Dedicated/private are in SOWs. Internal summary for sales: https://redwood.internal/sla-summary

Emily: Who owns the evals and prompt sets for regression monitoring? Research or Product?

Priya: Shared ownership: Research manages the harness and metrics, Product maintains prompt sets and acceptance criteria, Eng + SRE own rollout automation. We'll add a RACI to the playbook.

Lee: Can oncall rollback without PM approval during incidents?

Ingrid: Yes. Rollback authority is delegated to oncall when the incident meets severity thresholds in the runbook. Notify PMs ASAP but do not wait for approval.

Matt: Will there be an office hours session to walk through the playbook?

Ingrid: Yes 145-min office hours next Wed 4pm PT to go over details. Calendar: https://calendar.internal/event/eng-playbook-qa. Priya will update the playbook with the canary numbers and RACI by EOD Friday. Sofia will post the oncall rota template after office hours.

Emily: Thanks, will review and open any follow-ups on the doc. :thumbsup:

Ingrid: Thanks everyone. If I missed anything tag me and I'll add it to the playbook.
